Let \(A\) be the origin, and set

\[
\mathbf b=\overrightarrow{AB},\qquad \mathbf c=\overrightarrow{AC},\qquad \mathbf p=\overrightarrow{AP}.
\]

Since the tetrahedron is regular with edge length \(1\),

\[
|\mathbf b|=|\mathbf c|=|\mathbf p|=1,
\]
and each pair has angle \(60^\circ\), so

\[
\mathbf b\cdot \mathbf c=\mathbf c\cdot \mathbf p=\mathbf p\cdot \mathbf b=\frac12.
\]

Parameterize the points:

\[
E=x\mathbf p,
\]
\[
F=(1-y)\mathbf p+y\mathbf b,
\]
\[
G=z\mathbf c,
\]
\[
H=(1-s)\mathbf c+s\mathbf b.
\]

Then

\[
\overrightarrow{EF}=F-E=y\mathbf b+(1-y-x)\mathbf p,
\]

and

\[
\overrightarrow{GH}=H-G=s\mathbf b+(1-s-z)\mathbf c.
\]

Given

\[
\overrightarrow{EF}+\overrightarrow{GH}=\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf b,
\]

equating coefficients in the independent basis \(\mathbf b,\mathbf c,\mathbf p\) gives

\[
y+s=1,\qquad 1-y-x=0,\qquad 1-s-z=0.
\]

Let \(t=y\). Then

\[
s=1-t,\qquad x=1-t,\qquad z=t.
\]

Thus, with \(a=1-t\),

\[
E=a\mathbf p,
\]
\[
F=a\mathbf p+t\mathbf b,
\]
\[
G=t\mathbf c,
\]
\[
H=a\mathbf b+t\mathbf c.
\]

Now

\[
\overrightarrow{EH}=H-E=a\mathbf b+t\mathbf c-a\mathbf p,
\]

and

\[
\overrightarrow{FG}=G-F=-t\mathbf b+t\mathbf c-a\mathbf p.
\]

Using the dot-product relation for vectors in this basis,

\[
(\alpha\mathbf b+\beta\mathbf c+\gamma\mathbf p)\cdot(\alpha'\mathbf b+\beta'\mathbf c+\gamma'\mathbf p)
=
\frac12\bigl((\alpha+\beta+\gamma)(\alpha'+\beta'+\gamma')+\alpha\alpha'+\beta\beta'+\gamma\gamma'\bigr),
\]

we get

\[
\overrightarrow{EH}\cdot\overrightarrow{FG}
=
\frac12(a-t)^2
=
\frac12(1-2t)^2.
\]

Given that this equals \(\frac1{18}\),

\[
\frac12(1-2t)^2=\frac1{18}
\]

so

\[
(1-2t)^2=\frac19.
\]

Hence

\[
1-2t=\pm \frac13,
\]

giving

\[
t=\frac13 \quad\text{or}\quad t=\frac23.
\]

Now compute the desired dot product:

\[
\overrightarrow{EG}=G-E=t\mathbf c-a\mathbf p,
\]

and

\[
\overrightarrow{FH}=H-F=(a-t)\mathbf b+t\mathbf c-a\mathbf p.
\]

Their dot product is

\[
\overrightarrow{EG}\cdot\overrightarrow{FH}
=
\frac12\left(a^2+t^2\right)
=
\frac12\left((1-t)^2+t^2\right).
\]

For either \(t=\frac13\) or \(t=\frac23\),

\[
(1-t)^2+t^2=\frac49+\frac19=\frac59.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\overrightarrow{EG}\cdot\overrightarrow{FH}
=
\frac12\cdot\frac59
=
\frac5{18}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{5}{18}}
\]
